classification.difficultyReason: This is the same impossible-triangle idea as p68-q7, but the student has to decide to use the sine rule with the side opposite the 35° angle. The result sinB ≈ 1.27 > 1 must then be interpreted. That is still easier than finding the two SSA angles in p67-q1.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin B}{20}&=\frac{\sin35^{\circ}}{9}\\\sin B&=\frac{20\sin35^{\circ}}{9}\\\sin B&\approx1.27\end{align*}$$
A sine value cannot exceed $1$, so there is no angle $B$ and the triangle cannot exist.
